## Code description

The replication package contains a multi-step Stata/R/Fortran pipeline: multiple Stata do-files, including main files `master_synth.do`, `master.do`, and `produce_exhibits.do`; one R helper for Figure B9; and Fortran model code organized into 31 scenario folders.

{{< include generated/report-cloc.md >}}

- [x] The replication package contains a "main" or "master" file(s) which calls all other auxiliary programs.

## Computing Environment of the Replicator

- Nuvolos Cloud, Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS, 16-core CPU, 64 GB RAM, 50 GB storage
- Stata/MP 19.5
- R 4.5.1

For Fortran model replication only:

- MacBook M2 Pro with MacOS Tahoe 26.5.1 with 16 GB RAM

# Replication

- Downloaded code and data from dropbox.

- Opened Stata, changed directory to the root of the package and ran `synthetic_data/code/make_simulated_data.do` to regenerate the public dataset.

- As per Readme, ran `code/master_synth.do`. Several fixes needed to be applied, as described in the following points.

- Code initially failed due to missing packages `blindschemes` and `require` not recalled by authors. Packages were installed and code was relaunched.

```stata
. set scheme plotplain
scheme plotplain not found
r(111);
```

```stata
. reghdfe salary_r, a(district_code##year exp##masterup) resid
reghdfe requires uses the require package to maintain its dependencies; please install it:
 - install from SSC
 - install from GitHub
r(9);
```

- Ran `code/Figure_B9/cutoff_prefs_id_example_graph.R` as per Readme.

- Replicated locally (on MacOS) one single scenario (`1_baseline`) computed by the Model Code. 

- After having checked that the generated results for the replicated scenario matched those computed by authors, the pre-computed results were used to proceed with the last step of the replication (`code/produce_exhibits.do`).

- Code ran to completion.

# Classification

- [ ] full reproduction
- [ ] full reproduction with minor issues
- [x] partial reproduction (see above)
- [ ] not able to reproduce most or all of the results (reasons see above)

## Reason for incomplete reproducibility

- [ ] None.
- [ ] `Discrepancy in output` (either figures or numbers in tables or text differ)
- [ ] `Bugs in code` that were fixable by the replicator (but should be fixed in the final deposit)
- [x] `Code missing`, in particular if it prevented the replicator from completing the reproducibility check
  - [ ] `Data preparation code missing` should be checked if the code missing seems to be data preparation code
- [ ] `Code not functional` is more severe than a simple bug: it prevented the replicator from completing the reproducibility check
- [ ] `Software not available to replicator` may happen for a variety of reasons, but in particular (a) when the software is commercial, and the replicator does not have access to a licensed copy, or (b) the software is open-source, but a specific version required to conduct the reproducibility check is not available.
- [ ] `Insufficient time available to replicator` is applicable when (a) running the code would take weeks or more (b) running the code might take less time if sufficient compute resources were to be brought to bear, but no such resources can be accessed in a timely fashion (c) the replication package is very complex, and following all (manual and scripted) steps would take too long.
- [ ] `Data missing` is marked when data *should* be available, but was erroneously not provided, or is not accessible via the procedures described in the replication package
- [x] `Data not available` is marked when data requires additional access steps, for instance purchase or application procedure. 
- [ ] `Missing README` is marked if there is no README to guide the replicator, or the README is not in compliance with JPE requirements
